*Thinking as the farmer...*

Eh, let me think about this year. I've been farming this 9 mu for a long time, and I don't change much from year to year unless something goes wrong. What works works.

I split my land like I always do — about 4 mu for cotton on the drier piece, and the other 5 mu I do wheat and then maize after. That way we have grain for the family (six mouths, though the young ones buy some rice from town now with their wages) and cotton for cash. If cotton is bad one year, at least we eat. That's how my father did it and how I do it.

**Cotton, 4 mu** — I'll start preparing the ground in April when the soil warms. I buy seed from the town shop, the kind most people around here use, about 30 yuan worth per mu. Before planting I spread two bags of compound fertilizer across my four mu — that's one bag every two mu — and then when the cotton starts budding in June-July I put down urea, maybe half a bag per mu. My neighbor Old Wang tried using less last year and his bolls were small, so I won't cut back. Cotton drinks a lot of water and the bollworms are terrible — I'll spray maybe five or six times through the summer, whatever the shop tells me when I see the bugs. I water once after planting if it's dry, and maybe once more at flowering. Picking cotton takes the whole family — my wife, my older daughter when she comes back, me. Three pickings usually, into October. Hard work. If I get 250 jin of lint per mu I'm happy — last year was maybe a bit less because of that dry spell in August.

**Wheat, 5 mu** — Plant in October after I clear the maize stalks. I'll hire the small tractor from my cousin to plow, costs me maybe 40 yuan per mu. Seed I saved some from last year, plus buy a bit to mix. Before planting I spread compound fertilizer, one bag for every two mu, and then in March when the wheat is coming up and jointing I topdress with urea, maybe one bag per two mu. I irrigate three times — once before winter so it doesn't dry out, once in spring at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. Water from the well, costs me money to pump, that's why I don't do four times like the big farmers. Harvest is June with the combine, pay per mu. Last year I got about 400 jin per mu, hoping for the same.

**Maize, 5 mu** — Right after wheat harvest, no time to waste, maybe 2-3 days between. I direct seed into the stubble with a little machine, no plowing — there's no time for that in summer. Hybrid seed from the shop, about 80 yuan worth per mu because you can't save maize seed, it won't come right. Fertilizer goes in when planting, compound, and if the maize yellows in July I put urea on. Usually I water once at the big-leaf stage if the rains are late. Not much pesticide unless the borers are bad. Harvest end of September, maybe 450 jin per mu if the weather is good.

Money is always tight. The off-farm income from my son-in-law and my daughter helps us get through. I try not to borrow for inputs — cash in hand, spend only what you have. I don't do anything fancy. Same as last year, mostly.
